about:
Mahogany House Woodworks, operating as Boise Custom Furniture, is based in Nampa, Idaho. The company was founded in 2001 by James Barrett, who brought a background in construction and high-end custom home building to woodworking. Barrett runs the shop full-time while also owning a Boise HVAC repair business.

The shop designs and builds custom wood furniture including dining tables, coffee tables, beds, headboards, bookshelves, entryway tables, adjustable desks, workstations, and custom pieces for restaurants. They also produce wood countertops, butcher blocks, cutting boards, and offer furniture engraving. The operation is owner-operated; no facility size or headcount figures are disclosed.

Customers range from residential clients in Idaho and surrounding areas to commercial accounts such as restaurants and offices. Projects have included a large bookcase for a home, a bar top for a commercial space, and custom cutting boards for gifts.

Barrett emphasizes handcrafted methods and responsible material use as a response to mass-produced furniture. The company positions its work as heirloom-quality pieces built to last generations, with design guidance provided throughout the process.

name: Bond's Brewing Company-Buffalo
old_description: At Bond’s Brewing Company, our standard beers offer a little something for everyone, ensuring that every guest finds a brew they love. Crafted with high-quality ingredients, each beer highlights our dedication to excellence and balance. We strive to keep these favorites on tap year-round, providing a consistent selection of well-crafted brews that you can count on for any occasion.
about:
Founded in 2019 in Laramie, Wyoming, Bond's Brewing Company began as a craft brewery focused on unique, high-quality beer and a welcoming community space. The founders, whose names are not publicly disclosed, built the business around the idea that beer is an experience that brings people together.

The company operates two taprooms—in Laramie and, since a 2023 expansion, in Buffalo—where it produces a rotating lineup of year-round standard beers and seasonal releases. At the Buffalo location, the menu also includes expertly crafted cocktails made from fresh ingredients such as clam juice, tomatoes, and pickle juice. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Bond's Brewing serves local residents and visitors directly through its taprooms, offering a range of styles from a light kolsch-style ale to a hop-forward pale ale and fruit-infused wheat beers. The beers carry names like Arrowhead Red, Rhuberry, and Citra-Hop-A-Dopolis, reflecting regional inspiration and ingredient-driven recipes.

The company emphasizes its dedication to innovation, quality, and community, describing its spaces as gathering places that contribute to Wyoming's growing craft beverage scene. It highlights its award-winning beer and the introduction of craft cocktails as key differentiators.

name: BorgWarner Inc.
old_description: Industrial applications are evolving - and so are we. BorgWarner applies deep engineering expertise and advanced manufacturing capabilities to deliver solutions tailored to today’s industrial performance requirements.
about:
BorgWarner Inc., headquartered in Hanover Park, Illinois, is a global manufacturer of propulsion and energy storage systems. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure.

The company designs and manufactures battery energy storage systems (BESS), generator battery systems, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units, and turbine generator systems. Its production footprint spans North America and Europe, with over 5 GWh of annual battery production capacity. BorgWarner provides full mechanical, electrical, testing, and validation capabilities, along with engineering services and a cell-agnostic hardware and software architecture.

BorgWarner serves industrial customers requiring resilient energy storage, grid-scale energy storage, backup power, and power generation solutions. Its modular platforms address applications from rack-level backup to multi-megawatt-hour installations, supporting energy optimization and grid interaction.

BorgWarner emphasizes its automotive-grade battery technology, chemistry-independent platform, and global supply base for robust cell and component sourcing. The company also offers remanufacturing services to extend product life, aiming for long service life, high availability, and predictable performance in demanding industrial applications.

name: Boston Electronics
old_description: SiC photodiode UV sensors and probes meet the demanding needs for lamp monitoring and control in water, air, sun, surface, curing and instrument applications.
about:
Boston Electronics operates from Brookline, Massachusetts, where it has served the electro-optics market for four decades. The business is a tradename of 49Chestnut LLC, a Massachusetts limited liability company, and has been owned by Fiber Optic Center, Inc. No individual founders are named in the available records.

The company distributes advanced electro-optical components and specialized systems for microscopy and research. Its portfolio spans photon-counting modules, ultraviolet and infrared detectors, quantum cascade lasers, terahertz sources and imagers, and laboratory instrumentation such as blackbody calibration sources and laser power sensors. Boston Electronics maintains a web store with filtering tools for product selection and provides application engineering support to help customers integrate these components into their own designs.

Customers come from environmental monitoring, process control, scientific instrumentation, life sciences and biomedical technology, building and home automation, and security and surveillance. The company also supports academic and government research programs, including collaborations with organizations such as MIT's Advanced LIGO group and the Society for Neuroscience.

Boston Electronics states that its purpose is to enable customers to develop superior products and perform leading-edge research by supplying a broad range of advanced electro-optical solutions backed by knowledgeable application support. It emphasizes long-standing relationships with specialized manufacturers worldwide to bring advantaged, high-performance products to market.

name: Boulder Furniture Arts
old_description: HEY, WE'RE BFA — CHAMPIONS OF SIMPLICITY, BASED IN BOULDER SINCE 1985. OUR FURNITURE IS BUILT FROM UNMATCHED AMERICAN HARDWOOD AND DESIGNED FOR LIFELONG JOY.
about:
Boulder Furniture Arts, founded in 1985, operates from Boulder, Colorado. The company has built a reputation over nearly four decades as a fine furniture design-and-build studio.

The firm produces two primary lines: BFA Classic, a collection of time-honored designs largely unchanged since its inception, and BFA Create, a custom arm that develops one-off pieces, live-edge slabs, built-ins, and full installations. Work flows through an in-house process that includes concept development, CAD drawings and renderings, fabrication under a one-person-one-piece model, hand-rubbed oil finishing, and custom finish matching. The shop also offers commercial-grade options, built-and-brought delivery, full-service installation, and a lifetime guarantee backed by repair, refinishing, and disassembly services.

Clients range from architects who value precision to the 64th of an inch, interior designers seeking seamless collaboration, and residential customers furnishing homes with locally sourced hardwoods. The company also serves commercial leaders, artists, and environmentally conscious buyers who track carbon storage in their furnishings.

Boulder Furniture Arts distinguishes itself by sourcing all materials within a two-day drive of its shop, maintaining a ten-year apprenticeship program, and avoiding surplus inventory. The company describes itself as an old-school working art house run by people who give a damn, emphasizing analog modern design and playful restraint.

about:
Based in Dover, New Hampshire, Boulder Technologies, LLC operates as an independent distributor of board-level electronic components. The company was founded with over 25 years of combined industry experience among its team, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names have not been released.

The firm provides flexible, value-added distribution services tailored to dynamic market conditions. Its offerings include excess inventory management, outright purchase programs for idle stock, and aggressive sourcing of integrated circuits and passive components. Boulder Technologies maintains a stock of RoHS-compliant parts and emphasizes counterfeit mitigation across its supply chain.

Customers span electronic manufacturers, contract manufacturers, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), and telecommunication equipment producers. The company positions itself as a strategic partner for these sectors, leveraging its market knowledge and facilities to meet individual customer needs.

Boulder Technologies differentiates itself through its independent status, combined decades of buying and selling expertise, and a commitment to standing behind every component sold. The company was established to serve as a reliable, single-source partner capable of navigating complex component markets while guarding against fraud and unscrupulous practices.

name: Boxcar Woody (Reclaimed Lumber)
old_description: During those pioneering years, one car stood out among the rest, almost as important as the locomotive engine itself: the boxcar. Not just because of the versatility for the freight it could carry, but because of the connection with humanity it offered. The typical boxcar doubled as a passenger car for the ticketless. It was even sometimes left behind in those newly founded towns as a shelter or, for others, a home. It provided an escape for those wanting to run from his or her current predicament or a ride to a better life. Often, the boxcar’s walls were a sounding board for a newly penned song or where a life drew its very first and, sometimes, sadly, last breath. The American Boxcar was all of this and more to both early Americans and Immigrants alike.
about:
Boxcar Woody operates from Stockyards City in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The business traces its roots to 2015, when a road trip to harvest materials from retired American boxcars sparked the creation of Boxcar Revival, which later evolved into Boxcar Woody. The company remains privately held, though no specific ownership structure or founder names are disclosed publicly.

The company reclaims authentic freight materials—boxcar flooring, cargo planks, and whiskey barrel staves—and processes them in its Oklahoma workshop. Operations include selecting, milling, and finishing reclaimed lumber to produce raw materials such as countertop slabs, mantels, and flooring, as well as finished goods like dining tables, chairs, barstools, lighting fixtures, and barn doors. Each piece is handcrafted, and custom sizing is available for made-to-order projects.

Boxcar Woody serves residential and commercial customers, including homeowners, interior designers, and contractors. Projects range from whole-house remodels featuring countertops, sliding doors, and vanities to custom barn doors and hospitality installations such as bars with waterfall edges. Testimonials reference clients in Oklahoma and beyond who have used the material for furniture, countertops, and architectural elements.

The company states its mission is to preserve the history of American railways by giving retired boxcar materials new life in modern spaces. It emphasizes quality, craftsmanship, and the uniqueness of each piece, noting that no two tables are alike because the wood carries the character of its original service.

old_description: Boyko Inc. was formed in August of 1987 as a USDA food manufacturing plant. The company was founded by brothers Ron and Tom Boyko. Boyko Inc. has worked with numerous clients in developing and manufacturing products that are well suited for their individual needs. about:
Boyko Inc. was established in August 1987 in Stanton, North Dakota, by brothers Ron and Tom Boyko as a USDA-inspected food manufacturing plant producing bakery and meat products. The family-owned corporation quickly expanded its product development and manufacturing services for a variety of clients.

After years of growth, the company began upgrading its own equipment and found a market for the used machinery it replaced. In 1996 Boyko Inc. started buying and selling used food processing equipment, and by 2002 it had transitioned to full-time equipment dealing while still running the manufacturing plant. The manufacturing division was sold in 2006 to focus entirely on the used equipment business. Today the firm operates as a dealer and service provider, offering auctions, liquidations, consignment sales, asset management, process and plant system consulting, and technical support for food processing equipment.

The company serves food manufacturers and processors across the industry, helping them acquire or dispose of equipment ranging from bakery and packaging lines to conveyors, freezers, and mixers. Its customer base includes plants seeking individual machines, complete production lines, or turnkey liquidation services.

Drawing on its manufacturing heritage, Boyko Inc. emphasizes a practical understanding of processors' operational challenges. Its stated mission is to provide efficient, reliable service with integrity as a family-owned leader in the food processing sector.
